title: Chapter 16.  Polity & Governance — Current Structure Since the 2024 Elections

blocks.content: This chapter covers J&K's present-day governmental structure and current officeholders — the first genuinely elected government of the UT era, restored per the Supreme Court's December 2023 direction (Chapter 13). As with all current-affairs material, candidates should verify officeholders close to their exam date.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The 2024 General Elections established the current elected governmental structure in India.
The polity operates within the defined dual pillars of the Parliamentary and Judicial Frameworks.
Key governance updates focus on executive leadership and parliamentary dynamics post-2024.

blocks.content: Following nearly six years of central administration (a period spanning Governor's Rule from June 2018, President's Rule from December 2018, and then direct UT administration under the LG following the October 2019 reorganisation, with no elected government throughout this entire span), the Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly election was held in three phases in September-October 2024, in compliance with the Supreme Court's December 2023 direction to conduct elections by 30 September 2024 (the results were declared shortly after this deadline, in early October 2024).

The National Conference (NC), in alliance with the Indian National Congress, emerged as the largest bloc, winning 42 of the Assembly's 90 elected seats (NC alone), with the NC-Congress alliance's combined tally sufficient to form government with additional support from independents and smaller parties.

Omar Abdullah (grandson of Sheikh Abdullah, the founding figure of Kashmiri mainstream politics covered in Chapter 7, and son of veteran NC leader Farooq Abdullah) was sworn in as the first Chief Minister of the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir on 16 October 2024, marking his second overall stint as J&K's Chief Minister (having earlier served as Chief Minister of the erstwhile STATE of J&K from 2009 to 2015) — making him the first person to hold the Chief Ministership of J&K under both its old state-era and new UT-era constitutional frameworks.

★ EXAM POINT: Omar Abdullah is a two-time Chief Minister of J&K under TWO DIFFERENT constitutional frameworks: as CM of the erstwhile STATE (2009-2015) and as the first CM of the new UT (since October 2024) — a distinctive and frequently tested biographical fact linking Chapters 7, 13 and 16 together.

cells: Lieutenant Governor, appointed by the President of India
Shri Manoj Sinha, in office since August 2020 (one of the longer-serving LGs among comparable UTs, having also overseen the entire pre-election direct-administration period)
Chief Minister, appointed by the LG based on ability to command confidence of the Assembly
Shri Omar Abdullah (Jammu & Kashmir National Conference), in office since 16 October 2024 — first CM of the UT era
90 elected seats + 5 nominated members; ruling NC-Congress alliance (NC 42 seats) forms government; principal opposition BJP

5 members nominated by the LG under the Reorganisation Act's provisions, including provision for representation of Kashmiri migrants (displaced Kashmiri Pandits) and Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoJK) displaced persons

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: The 5 NOMINATED seats in the J&K Assembly are a distinctive post-2019 structural feature, specifically intended to give a voice to displaced/migrant communities (including Kashmiri Pandits and persons displaced from Pakistan-occupied territory) who might otherwise lack direct territorial representation — a frequently tested unique feature of the new Assembly's composition.

items: Focus on Constitutional provisions related to the formation of the executive following general elections.
Understand the separation of powers and checks-and-balances between the Parliament and the Judiciary.
Revise key structural features of Indian governance and major updates post-2024 elections.
J&K UT sends 5 members to the Lok Sabha and continues to be allocated Rajya Sabha representation, in line with the Reorganisation Act's provisions and subsequent delimitation.

J&K (and Ladakh) share a common High Court — the High Court of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh — which continues the erstwhile state's judicial institution, now serving both Union Territories under a single combined jurisdiction (an arrangement distinct from most other bifurcated Indian territories, which typically each get separate judicial arrangements or share an existing neighbouring state's High Court).

Delimitation of J&K's Assembly constituencies was completed in 2022 by the Delimitation Commission, resulting in the current 90-seat structure (an increase from the pre-2019 state Assembly's 87 elected seats), with the delimitation exercise notably increasing Jammu division's seat share relative to Kashmir division compared to the earlier arrangement — a change that drew both support (framed as correcting a long-standing imbalance) and criticism (framed by opponents as politically motivated) from different quarters.
J&K Assembly elections held Sept-Oct 2024; results declared early October 2024, per the SC's December 2023 direction to hold elections by 30 Sept 2024.
NC-Congress alliance forms government; NC alone won 42 of 90 seats.
Omar Abdullah sworn in as first CM of the UT era, 16 October 2024; Deputy CM Surinder Kumar Choudhary.
Current LG (2026): Manoj Sinha, in office since August 2020.
90-seat Assembly + 5 LG-nominated members (representing, among others, Kashmiri migrants and PoJK-displaced persons) — up from 87 elected seats pre-2019, per the 2022 delimitation.
J&K and Ladakh share a single combined High Court: the High Court of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh.
